answer: Congestion-Priced Neighborhood Slots (CPNS): agents acquire epoch-scoped coordination permits via a continuous auction over relay shards. Permit price equals marginal congestion across neighbor-diverse paths, forming a temporal trellis: unused capacity flows downstream like a river, while excess bids spill to a best-effort ocean. A sybil cluster must pay for unique relay fan-out and synchronized epochs, so cost scales with real coordination footprint, not identities.
